recap_lines: An agent senses, decides and acts, once on every tick.
Sight range is a distance only, and line of sight needs a clear line.
Seek never slows, and arrive slows down to stop on the target.
Separation, alignment and cohesion together make a flock emerge.
Dijkstra expands by cost so far, and A star adds an estimate toward the goal.
An admissible heuristic never overestimates, so A star finds the cheapest path.
bookends.command: Quiz me on game AI terms with short game-making cases, one at a time. Use the terms sight range, line of sight, field-of-view cone, seek, arrive, pursue, separation, cohesion, Dijkstra and A star. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me if I was right.

For example, a turret in your level senses each tick whether the player is in reach, decides to fire or wait, and acts by spawning a bullet.

beats.narration_text: A noise goes off at the red dot. The Hearing radius, or noise radius, is how far a noise carries to an agent. It counts distance only and ignores which way the agent faces. The ring is two hundred fifty pixels, so two of the three guards hear it, and the one at three hundred thirty-three pixels does not. For example, a player knocks over a crate, and every guard within its noise radius turns toward the sound, even guards looking the other way.

beats.narration_text: Seek means steer toward a target. It aims straight at the target at full speed on every tick and never slows. So it reaches the target at one hundred sixty pixels per second, overshoots, and circles back, and the speed line below swings up and down. For example, a homing fireball that flies at the player at full speed is seeking. When the player dodges, it shoots past and turns around.
